record.paper_title: Twenty open problems in quantum control
record.context_brief: Limits of linear networks for quantum error correction
record.original_question: For linear quantum systems coupled irreversibly through quantum fields, also called quantum linear networks, can one prove that such linear networks cannot implement quantum error correction, meaning correction of errors on arbitrary unknown quantum states?

evidence.quote: A subset of CFC problems that is being investigated by a number of groups from the control theory community is that of linear quantum systems coupled (irreversibly) via quantum fields. These systems are also referred to as quantum linear networks.
Problem 10: Show that linear networks cannot perform quantum error-correction.
Error-correction involves correcting errors on arbitrary states, that is states about which the error correcting process is ignorant.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider linear quantum systems that are coupled irreversibly to one another through bosonic quantum fields (quantum linear networks). Concretely, such a system consists of a finite collection of quantum harmonic oscillators with quadratic Hamiltonians and linear couplings to input/output bosonic field channels, governed by quantum stochastic differential equations whose Heisenberg dynamics preserve the linear span of the canonical position and momentum (quadrature) operators. Quantum error correction means a procedure that, given an arbitrary unknown quantum state subjected to an error from a specified error class, recovers the original state without requiring prior knowledge of that state.

Problem: Prove (or disprove) that no quantum linear network of the above form can implement quantum error correction; that is, show that within the class of linear quantum systems coupled through quantum fields there exists no encoding-decoding scheme capable of correcting errors on arbitrary unknown quantum states.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted search did not surface a definitive impossibility theorem establishing that linear quantum networks cannot perform quantum error correction on arbitrary unknown states. Related work investigates passive error correction of linear optics networks via unitary/error averaging and feedback-based schemes, but these address restricted error/state classes rather than refuting or confirming the general impossibility claim. The status therefore appears unresolved in the publicly available literature found.

status_evidence.title: Passive quantum error correction of linear optics networks through error averaging
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes error detection/correction for bosonic linear networks using unitary averaging, without ancillary photons or feedforward.
status_evidence.claim: Work on linear-network error mitigation exists but does not prove the general impossibility for arbitrary unknown states.

status_evidence.title: Quantum error correction for communication with linear optics
status_evidence.snippet: Schemes combining linear optics with feedback/measurement can correct certain noise classes.
status_evidence.claim: Linear-optics-based correction schemes exist for restricted models, leaving the general question about purely linear networks unsettled.
